q: What is the unit of energy?
What is the unit of power?
What is the unit of force?
Name the 8 energy stores.
What energy store does a stretched spring have?
a: The spring stores energy when deformed and releases it when it returns to shape.

q: What is the difference between a STORE and a PATHWAY?
a: Store = where energy is held (e.g. kinetic, thermal)
Pathway = HOW energy moves between stores

q: Name the 4 energy transfer pathways.
Is radiation a store or a pathway?
a: Radiation (infrared, light) is a mechanism of energy transfer.
Thermal is the store; radiation is how energy travels.

q: Write the energy chain for a burning candle.
Write the energy chain for an electric kettle.
Write the energy chain for a ball falling.
Write the energy chain for a wind turbine.
State the Law of Conservation of Energy.
a: Energy cannot be created or destroyed.
It can only be transferred from one store to another.
Total energy of a closed system is always constant.

q: What is energy dissipation?
a: Energy spreading out into the thermal store of the surroundings.
Dissipated energy is less useful — e.g. heat from friction.
Dissipation is why 100% efficiency is impossible.

q: State the formula for efficiency.
a: Efficiency = Useful Energy Output ÷ Total Energy Input
As decimal (0 to 1) or ×100 for percentage (0% to 100%).

q: A motor uses 400J and produces 280J useful KE. What is the efficiency?
An LED is 35% efficient and uses 60J. Find useful output.
What is a Sankey diagram?
a: Width of arrow ∝ amount of energy.
Wasted outputs → branch up or down

q: How does CONDUCTION transfer thermal energy?
a: Vibrating particles collide with neighbours, passing energy along.
Does NOT require the medium to move.

q: How does CONVECTION transfer thermal energy?
a: Only in LIQUIDS and GASES — not solids.

q: How does RADIATION transfer thermal energy?
a: No medium needed — works in a VACUUM.

q: Which surface is the best absorber of radiation?
a: Also the BEST emitter of radiation.
Shiny/white surfaces are the WORST absorbers and emitters.

q: What are TWO ways to reduce energy transfer by conduction?
a: Air is an excellent thermal insulator.

q: State the required practical for thermal energy transfer.
a: Heater in water + ammeter (series) + voltmeter (parallel) + thermometer.

q: State the formula for work done.
a: d = distance in direction of force (metres, m)

q: When is work NOT done on an object?
a: When the force is PERPENDICULAR to the displacement.
e.g. Carrying a bag horizontally — upward force ⊥ horizontal motion → no work done against gravity.
Also: no movement → no work done.

q: A 50N force moves a box 8m. Calculate the work done.
a: 400 joules of energy is transferred to the box.

q: A person of weight 700N climbs 5m of stairs. What is the work done against gravity?
Where does the work done against friction go?
a: All the work done against friction becomes
It cannot be recovered as useful work.

q: Define work done in physics.
a: Work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force.
Work done is equal to the energy transferred.

sections.title: Power: P = W/t and P = Fv

q: Define power and state its unit.
a: More powerful = does SAME work in LESS time.

q: State the two formulae for power.
a: Derived: P = W/t → W=Fd → P = Fd/t → P = Fv

q: A crane does 36,000J of work in 60s. Calculate the power.
A car exerts 4000N at 25m/s. Calculate the power.
A 2.4kW motor runs for 5 minutes. How much energy is transferred?
A pump produces 6kW of power. Water flows at 3m/s. Find the force.
a: P = F × v → F = P ÷ v

q: State the formula for gravitational potential energy.
What value of g should you use in IGCSE calculations?
a: (unless the question states a different value)
This is the gravitational field strength on Earth.

q: Calculate GPE: m = 5kg, h = 8m, g = 10N/kg.
At what height is GPE = zero?
a: GPE is measured relative to a chosen reference level, usually the ground.

q: If mass doubles, what happens to GPE?
a: If height doubles, GPE also doubles.

q: A 2kg book is on a shelf 1.5m high. Calculate its GPE.
State the formula for kinetic energy.
What happens to KE when speed doubles?
a: This is why speeding is so dangerous.

q: Calculate KE: m = 1500kg, v = 20m/s.
State the relationship when a ball falls freely (no friction).
a: Speed depends ONLY on height — NOT on mass.

q: A ball drops from 45m. Find its speed at the ground (g=10).
A 4kg ball is thrown up with KE = 320J. Find max height (g=10).
a: At max height: KE = 0 → all GPE

q: What is a non-renewable energy resource? Give examples.
a: A resource that CANNOT be replaced once used.
Examples: coal, oil, natural gas, nuclear fuel (uranium)

q: What is a renewable energy resource? Give examples.
a: A resource that will NOT run out.
Examples: wind, solar, hydroelectric, geothermal, tidal, wave

q: State the energy chain for a fossil fuel power station.
State TWO advantages and TWO disadvantages of nuclear power.
a: Advantages: No CO₂ · Huge energy output from small fuel
Disadvantages: Radioactive waste · Expensive to build · Risk of accident · Slow to start

q: Why is wind power described as intermittent?
a: Wind speed varies and may be zero.
When there is no wind → no electricity generated.

q: State the difference between solar cells and solar heating panels.
a: Solar cells: convert sunlight DIRECTLY to ELECTRICITY
Solar heating: heat water in pipes

q: Describe the National Grid sequence from power station to home.
Why is electricity transmitted at HIGH VOLTAGE?
a: Low current → less power wasted as heat in cables (P = I²R)
Makes transmission far more efficient over long distances.

q: What does a step-UP transformer do?
a: Used at the power station before long-distance transmission.

q: What does a step-DOWN transformer do?
a: Makes electricity safe for homes and offices.
Used at local substations near consumers.

q: Why must mains electricity be AC rather than DC?
a: Transformers need a CHANGING magnetic field to work.
Only AC creates a continuously changing field.
DC produces a constant magnetic field → transformer does not work.

q: State the mains supply values for UK households.
a: The current direction reverses 50 times per second.
